\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Threshold Functions --- Polynomial}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Polynomial
\section{Overview}
Walsh coefficient families evaluate to multilinear cube functions with the same Fourier coefficients. Their degree, correlation, norm, and threshold identities follow in this representation.

\difficulty{1}
For any natural number $n$, any real coefficient family $p$ indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and every subset $S$ of that coordinate set, the Fourier--Walsh
coefficient at $S$ of the polynomial represented by $p$ equals $p(S)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coefficient degree bounds Fourier degree]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.has_degree_at_most_eval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.fourierCoeff_eval, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b010,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b011,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p216-b001
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. If $k\ge0$ is an integer and $a_S=0$ whenever $|S|>k$, then $\widehat P(S)\ne0$ implies $|S|\le k$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For any natural number $n$ and any real coefficient family $p$ indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the uniform inner product of the polynomial represented by $p$ with
itself equals $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For any natural number $n$, any real coefficient family $p$ indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and any real-valued function $u$ on the Boolean cube, the uniform
inner product of the polynomial represented by $p$ with $u$ equals
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\widehat u(S)$, where $\widehat u(S)$ is the
Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $u$ at $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coefficient bound by absolute mean]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.abs_coeff_le_expect_abs}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.fourierCoeff_eval, BooleanAnalysis.chiS_sq_eq_one, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p$ assign a real coefficient $p(S)$ to each subset
$S\subseteq[n]$, and let $P(x)=\sum_{T\subseteq[n]}p(T)\chi_T(x)$ be its Walsh
expansion. For every $S\subseteq[n]$, \[|p(S)|\le\mathbb E_x|P(x)|,\] where the
expectation is uniform on the Boolean cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positive energy of a nonzero coefficient family]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.sum_sq_pos}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
For any natural number $n$ and any nonzero real coefficient family $p$ indexed by
subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the sum $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2$ is
strictly positive.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube. If $f(x)$
equals $1$ when the polynomial represented by $p$ is nonnegative at $x$, and equals $-1$
otherwise, then the uniform expectation of the absolute value of that polynomial equals
its uniform inner product with $f$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evaluation of a degree-one polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval_of_degree_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$,
and suppose $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. Then for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$,
\[\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)\chi_S(x)=p(\varnothing)+\sum_{i\in[n]}p(\{i\})(-1)^{x_i}.\]
\end{lemma}

  {BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval_sub}
  {context}
  {lmn-constant-depth-fourier}
  {pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b005}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$. Its Walsh–Fourier expansion recovers
$f$ at every point: \[f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x),\qquad
x\in\{0,1\}^n,\] where $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_y[f(y)\chi_S(y)]$ and $\chi_S$ is the
Walsh character.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evaluation of a polynomial difference]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval_sub}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval_sub}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $n$ and any two multilinear polynomials $F$ and $G$ on the
$n$-dimensional Boolean cube, the polynomial represented by their difference evaluates
at each point of the cube to the difference of their evaluations.
\end{lemma}
